q: 1. Accidental or compensating errors of length L are proportional to
explain: Accidental (compensating) errors accumulate in proportion to the square root of the total measured length L, following the statistical law of random errors.

q: 2. While measuring a chain line between two stations A and B intervened by a raised ground
options: both vision and chaining get obstructed
explain: A raised intervening ground obstructs both the line of sight between the two stations and the physical continuity of chaining across it, so both vision and chaining get obstructed.

q: 3. Prolongation of chain line across an obstruction in chain surveying, is done by
explain: Prolonging a chain line across an obstruction can be achieved using any of several field methods together - angular measurements, constructing perpendiculars, or solving triangles - so all of the above are valid techniques.

q: 4. In chain surveying tie lines are primarily provided
options: to check the accuracy of the survey
to take offsets for detail survey
to avoid long offsets from chain lines
to increase the number of chain lines
explain: The primary purpose of providing tie lines in chain surveying is to avoid having to take unduly long offsets directly from the main chain lines, by providing closer reference lines for nearby detail.

q: 5. In chain surveying field work is limited to
explain: Chain surveying, by its fundamental nature, restricts all field work to linear measurements only, without any angular measurement instruments being used.
A clinometer's specific and sole function is to measure the angle of slope (inclination) of the ground or a line of sight.
